introduction.heading: Plumbing for Orem homes
introduction.body:
Half of the homes in Orem were built in 1989 or later, and about 37% before 1980, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Many of those homes are reaching the age when water heaters, faucets and fixtures need replacing. A water heater usually lasts 10 to 15 years.

About 60% of Orem's water is surface water from the Provo River and the Deer Creek and Jordanelle reservoirs, treated at the Don A. Christiansen Regional Water Treatment Plant. The other 40% comes from nine deep wells and two mountain springs in Provo Canyon. Hardness ranges from 120 to 428 mg/L (7 to 25 grains per gallon) across the city's system, according to Orem's 2025 water quality report. The U.S. Geological Survey classes that as moderately hard to very hard water. Hard water leaves mineral deposits in water heaters, faucets and appliances, and a water softener or filtration system cuts that buildup.

Orem's service line inventory found no lead service lines, though 1,830 lines of unknown material still need to be identified.
